items.objective: Specify when bridge modules, reassessment, transcript movement, travel/accessibility accommodations, and other substitute-equivalent costs caused by a midstream rule change must be absorbed by the receiving/public system rather than charged back to the learner.
items.why_live: The archive now knows what counts as documented reliance and what burden bands trigger stronger protection, but it still lacks a sharper cross-sector rule for who pays when continuity still requires extra steps.

items.objective: Specify a promotion-and-retirement rule for starter override rows so institutions know when a provisional row should become a stronger sector default, split by age band or stakes, soften back toward protected default, or retreat to local-only publication.

items.objective: Specify a publication-and-activation profile for predeclared continuity reserves and published public entitlements so institutions know which trigger facts, proof minima, claiming windows, and coordination fields must be published once repeated `K2` / `K3` burdens stop living as ad hoc hardship handling.
items.why_live: The archive now knows which no-fault payer defaults harden by sector and when repeated support or cycle-loss burdens should graduate into reserves or entitlement floors, but it still lacks a disciplined answer about what reserve or entitlement notices must actually publish and what proof/window package truly travels across sectors.

items.objective: Specify when predeclared continuity reserves must escalate to a temporary stronger floor because the reserve is depleted, host capacity collapses, or several nodes each deny sole responsibility while the learner's continuity window is still live.
items.why_live: The archive now knows what reserve and entitlement notices must publish and how learners should activate them, but it still lacks a disciplined answer about what happens when a reserve runs short or a cross-node collision makes reserve-based handling too weak to keep continuity real.

items.objective: Specify which priority facts, batching rules, and learner-facing scarcity-publication fields in the `ES2` / `ES3` layer really harden across sectors, where office-, host-, or funder-specific law still forces local scarcity handling, and when temporary stronger-floor scarcity should itself graduate into a standing entitlement rather than recurring override work.
items.why_live: The archive now has a compact scarcity-escalation ladder and anti-race floor for reserve depletion, host-capacity strain, and cross-node responsibility disputes, but it still lacks the next narrower answer about which scarcity triage facts and publication duties truly travel once even the temporary stronger floor cannot serve everyone at once.

items.objective: Specify when repeated `ES2` / `ES3` scarcity on the same route should force predeclared multi-destination, shadow-capacity, or shared-slot planning, which minimal cross-node commitments really travel, and when recurring scarcity should remain temporary override rather than becoming preallocated continuity infrastructure.
items.why_live: The archive now knows which triage facts, batching rules, and scarcity-publication fields truly travel once a stronger floor is oversubscribed, but it still lacks the next narrower answer about when repeated stronger-floor use should be converted into predeclared capacity planning before the next disruption rather than rerun as emergency coordination.

items.objective: Specify which parts of predeclared multi-destination, shadow-capacity, and shared-slot continuity planning must be learner-visible, which may remain partner-facing, and how those arrangements should refresh, expire, or require republication before the next disruption.

items.objective: Specify which partner, route, timing, approval, or pricing changes inside a `CP1` / `CP2` / `CP3` planning layer are material enough to force fresh learner-facing republication, which may be handled through quiet partner-side reconfirmation only, and when a lapsed arrangement may still be used merely as a provisional lead rather than a live continuity promise.
items.why_live: The archive now knows which parts of predeclared continuity-capacity planning must be learner-visible, which may stay partner-facing, and how freshness should decay from `FS0` to `FS2`, but it still lacks the next narrower answer about which real-world changes cross the line from ordinary partner maintenance into learner-facing republication duty and provisional-use caution.

items.objective: Specify which `FS1` / provisional-lead states may still publish a named destination, which should collapse to destination-family or owner-contact-only shells, and where sector or posture differences force earlier downgrade before learner-facing continuity planning remains truthful.
items.why_live: The archive now distinguishes hidden maintenance from learner-facing material change and separates partner-only memory, family-only provisional leads, and rare named verify-on-activation leads, but it still lacks the next narrower answer about how much destination detail may remain learner-visible inside `FS1` by sector and continuity posture before provisional publication itself becomes misleading.

items.objective: Specify when learners who see only `DD1` or `DD2` continuity shells must receive a named destination, equivalent option set, or explicit no-route-yet notice after activation begins, and what acknowledgement / verification clocks should vary by sector and posture.
items.why_live: The archive now knows how much destination detail may remain learner-visible while a route stays in `FS1`, but it still lacks the next narrower answer about when provisional publication must turn into concrete named routing, equivalent-option disclosure, or an explicit failure-to-match notice once a real learner claim has actually activated.

items.objective: Specify what minimum comparability fields an `AR2` equivalent-option set must show, when route differences are too material for `AR2`, and when learner-choice windows or silent default assignment become coercive rather than continuity-preserving.

items.objective: Specify when `SW1-SW5` no-loss switch rights may narrow, expire, or convert into ordinary local route rules after onboarding, attendance, aid disbursement, host preparation, or partially consumed support, and what sunk-cost or consumed-capacity facts are strong enough to justify that narrowing without retroactive burden shift.

items.objective: Specify when a `TP2` or `TP3` continuity case must reopen fuller `SW1-SW5` protection because the assigned route later changes, worsens, or fails, and which post-start route deteriorations count as a fresh system-caused continuity event rather than ordinary learner progress risk.
